capabilities: Merge Markdown tables from many notes by matching column names
Sort rows by any column and filter rows with a find box
Add summary rows and group subtotals (Pro)
Roll up task lists from headings into Task, Done and Due columns (Pro)
Export the merged table to a new note or CSV file (Pro)
extras: Freemium: free tier merges up to 50 notes with sorting and search; Pro (GitHub Sponsors, $15 one-time or $5/month) removes the limit and adds summaries, filters, task rollup and export. After GitHub sign-in the plugin contacts GitHub to verify sponsorship; no note content is sent. Requires Obsidian 1.13.4 or later. Settings and a What's new tab promote other NoteMods plugins and a Telegram chat.
intentEvidence: Table Rollup is a view for the core Bases plugin. The base selects the notes, and Table Rollup draws one merged table
problem: Bases views work on note properties, so there is no built-in way to combine the contents of Markdown tables scattered across many notes into one merged, sortable view.

relations.evidence: Dataview reads properties and inline fields, not Markdown tables.
SQLSeal reads a Markdown table, but you write one query line for each file
Block View lists matching blocks from many notes, but it shows each table on its own

summary: Bases view that merges Markdown tables from many notes into one sortable table, matching columns by name and linking each row to its source note.
